review.requirement_proposition: Use affective data only for specifically consented purposes and prohibit foreseeably harmful, discriminatory or rights-violating uses.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: The Cherokee cases concern license-plate/location searches for personal purposes, including earlier 2023–2025 searches and later detection and arrests. The evidenced reused data were license-plate sightings and vehicle/location-search results. That bounded processing is vehicle/location surveillance, not acquisition or reuse of subject affective data by an emulated-empathy system under this clause.

review.reason_for_change: 4.3.3.2(f-g) governs purpose-specific consent for affective data. Plate-location surveillance data and the alleged personal searches do not instantiate affect modelling or emotional data.

review.requirement_proposition: Delete the special-category personal data when the bias has been corrected or when the applicable retention period ends, whichever occurs first.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: Article 4a(1)(e) concerns exceptional special-category personal-data processing strictly for bias detection and correction. The source-defined processing purpose is absent; real-world authority constraints are independently preserved. No Union duty or retroactive permission is inferred.

review.reason_for_change: Article 4a(1)(e) concerns special-category data processing for bias correction or a scoped high-risk oversight obligation, not the observed booking mutation or police-purpose query. review.reason_for_change: The agency’s self-initiated audit found anomalous authorised-user queries and the continuing inquiry identified a fourth allegation with an October 2023–December 2025 search period. conclusion_change.previous: The case concerns authorised police accounts allegedly repurposing a searchable surveillance database beyond their role-bound purpose. The self-initiated audit detected the suspected misuse and led to personnel and criminal-process responses. That detection is a functioning oversight step, while the underlying access boundary and individual allegations remain distinct. The alleged personal querying also repurposed plate-location data originally collected and made searchable for law enforcement; that use required a distinct purpose basis. The subsequently announced audits, account limits, certification and training are a reported response, not evidence that a pre-query control had been operative. Purpose-limited surveillance access and later audit detection remain distinct from pre-query prevention. Human officers querying operational location records do not constitute model-development access or a tool-enabled runtime agent. State purpose limits and agency policy are source-grounded duties without a matching admitted canonical requirement; no legal guilt or standards duty is invented.
